page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core processing is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% ratings in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside poor single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in multi-core workloads, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core execution, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains in the average tier for both cached and uncached operations, though the Passmark memory score falls into the weak category.

The instance provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It achieves average throughput in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and small-model LLM inference. Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.g5.6xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is best suited for multi-threaded applications, web serving, and database operations that can leverage the 24 dedicated vCPUs, while single-threaded tasks and memory-intensive operations may experience performance bottlenecks.
